references.text: Job describes those who are "enemies of the light" – those who do not know the ways of the light and refuse to walk in its paths. This directly reflects the thought in John 3:19 that people loved darkness rather than light because their deeds were evil.

John's prologue states that in the Word was life, and the life was the light of all people, and that the light shines in the darkness. John 1:4-5 lays the foundation for the judgment in John 3:19: the light has come into the world.

The true light that gives light to everyone came into the world, but the world did not know him, and his own people did not receive him (John 1:9-11). This is the same rejection of the light described in John 3:19.
Jesus proclaims "I am the light of the world" (John 8:12). This emphasizes that the "light" that has come into the world in John 3:19 is Jesus himself.

Jesus urges the crowd to believe in the light while they have it, so that they may become children of the light (John 12:35-36). The theme is the same as in John 3:19: the light is present, but people risk choosing darkness.

Jesus says he has come into the world as a light, so that no one who believes in him should remain in darkness (John 12:46-48). The word he has spoken will judge on the last day – parallel to the judgment in John 3:19.

Paul describes in Romans 1:21-23 how people, though they knew God, did not honor him or give thanks, but became futile in their thinking and exchanged the glory of the immortal God for images resembling mortal man. Their deliberate rejection of the truth they knew reflects the pattern in John 3:19.
Paul urges believers to cast off the works of darkness and put on the armor of light (Romans 13:12). The contrast between the deeds of darkness and the light reflects the theme in John 3:19.

Paul exhorts believers not to have fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness, but rather to expose them, for everything that is exposed by the light becomes visible (Ephesians 5:11-13). This explains why evil people flee from the light, as described in John 3:19.
Isaiah pronounces woe upon those who call darkness light and light darkness (Isaiah 5:20). This moral blindness is at the heart of the judgment described in John 3:19.

John writes that God is light, and in him there is no darkness at all. Whoever says they have fellowship with God yet walks in darkness lies (1 John 1:5-7). This expands on the connection between light, darkness, and deeds found in John 3:19.
The true light is already shining, and whoever hates their brother remains in darkness (1 John 2:8-11). Love of darkness is linked to evil deeds, as in John 3:19.
